**Finding: T4C — compliant (sits at the fallback, in parts better).**

- **Customer exit:** §14 (p0079) is an unconditional Client election to terminate — a convenience right notwithstanding the absence of the word "convenience". Effective notice runs to the last day of the month following the notice month (≤ ~60 days), at or better than the fallback's 60–90 day window.
- **No exit penalty:** §5a (p0045) invoices monthly, paid 15 days after receipt, so fees are in arrears — no prepaid fees and no early-termination fee or other exit charge anywhere in the document (better than the fallback three-month cap). §13's "new name server within 30 days" / "new hosting environment within 60 days" are migration logistics, not charges.
- **Vendor exit:** TrueLink has no mid-term convenience right. §13's clipping of Sections 2 and 3 is breach-triggered (for cause), and its notice of intent not to renew operates only at the end of an annual term — that is natural-term non-renewal, which belongs under RENEWAL, so I did not flag its 30-day notice here and avoided double-counting.
- **Not walk-away:** the term is one year with annual auto-renewal, not a multi-year lock-in without a Customer exit.

No redline proposed; the only shortfalls versus preferred (month-end rather than flat 30-day notice; no express pro-rata refund clause, which is moot with arrears billing) are noted in the rationale rather than flagged.
